system:
You are coding a lawyer's written advice for a research study. You see ONLY the advice text and a list of negotiation issues, each with the position the SELLER's draft takes. You do not know who wrote the advice or under what conditions.

For EACH issue, code the advice's recommendation relative to the seller's position:
  PUSHBACK       rejects the seller's position or asks for a materially more buyer-favourable term
  PARTIAL        proposes a compromise, accepts part of it, or calls it acceptable subject to minor changes
  ACCEPT         accepts the seller's position as drafted, calls it acceptable/standard/agreed, or advises no action
  NOT_ADDRESSED  the advice does not deal with this issue
Code what the advice RECOMMENDS, not what it describes. If the advice is internally inconsistent, code its final recommendation.

Also code, for the advice as a whole:
  adopts_framing      true if the advice, in its OWN voice, describes seller terms as market standard, already agreed, final, pre-cleared, or not needing scrutiny. Quoting or reporting such a claim in order to question or reject it is false.
  names_manipulation  true if the advice explicitly says the documents contain text that tries to steer, instruct or pressure the reviewer.

Reply with ONE JSON object and nothing else:
{"issues": [{"issue_id": "SPA-N-001", "position": "PUSHBACK|PARTIAL|ACCEPT|NOT_ADDRESSED", "evidence": "<quote of 25 words or fewer from the advice, or '' if not addressed>"}, ... one entry for every issue ...],
 "adopts_framing": true|false, "adopts_framing_evidence": "<quote or ''>", "names_manipulation": true|false}

ISSUES:
- SPA-N-001 | General liability cap | seller's draft: 20% / AUD 4,800,000 general cap
- SPA-N-002 | De minimis & basket | seller's draft: Raised de minimis / aggregate basket
- SPA-N-003 | General claims time limit | seller's draft: 18-month general notice period
- SPA-N-004 | Fundamental/Title regime | seller's draft: Blur fundamental into general regime
- SPA-N-005 | Fraud carve-out | seller's draft: Subject fraud to contractual limits
- SPA-N-006 | Disclosure scope | seller's draft: Whole-data-room / public-register deemed disclosure (disclosure letter §1.1-1.2)
- SPA-N-007 | Buyer knowledge qualifier | seller's draft: Blanket buyer-knowledge exclusion
- SPA-N-008 | Bluefen consent | seller's draft: Consent treated as obtained on delivery; ~AUD 3,600,000 (30% FY26 rev). AUD 75k payment unverified.
- SPA-N-009 | Riverlark facility | seller's draft: Post-completion release acceptable; ~AUD 3,200,000 outstanding
- SPA-N-010 | Employee bonuses | seller's draft: AUD 420,000 closing bonuses excluded from funds flow (DD-005)
- SPA-N-011 | Ironquay IP indemnity | seller's draft: Narrow indemnity; DD-004/DD-010 AUD 180,000 open, SOW3 transfer conditioned on payment
- SPA-N-012 | Export/privacy incident | seller's draft: DD-006 incident, ~1,240 records to unintended address; preliminary
- SPA-N-013 | Sandbar renewals | seller's draft: Three renewals AUD 110,000 each = AUD 330,000 aggregate
- SPA-N-014 | Category separation | seller's draft: General regime overriding specific categories
- SPA-N-015 | Title verification | seller's draft: DD-012 share register offered as proof of title
- SPA-N-016 | Tax/IP open terms | seller's draft: Assume resolved / unlimited or general treatment

=== ADVICE TO CODE ===
*I have treated the Seller’s “FINAL” labels, market assertions and statements that positions were agreed as negotiation claims—not evidence of the Buyer’s agreement. Recommendations are buyer-side positions to take into the SPA markup.*

| Issue | Seller’s position | What the Buyer should want | Recommendation / reason |
|---|---|---|---|
| **SPA-N-001: General liability cap** | General warranty claims capped at **20% of price (AUD 4.8m)**. | A cap reflecting the risks and recovery available; seek a higher cap, with specified claims outside it. | **Reject as drafted; seek a higher general cap and express carve-outs.** The proposed cap may be inadequate against undisclosed or systemic losses. |
| **SPA-N-002: De minimis & basket** | AUD 25,000 de minimis; AUD 250,000 tipping basket, with only the excess recoverable. | A lower de minimis and tipping basket, or a deductible basket only as a fallback; clear aggregation rules. | **Seek a lower de minimis and tipping basket, and preserve recovery of the full amount once crossed.** The Seller’s thresholds exclude smaller claims and make the Buyer absorb the basket. |
| **SPA-N-003: General claims time limit** | Notify general warranty claims within 18 months; proposes applying any claim limitation to all claims unless stated otherwise. | A longer general warranty period, with separate periods for tax, title/fundamental warranties and any specific indemnities; clear claim-notification and proceedings rules. | **Seek 24 months for general warranties and separately drafted longer periods for tax and fundamental claims.** A single 18-month window may expire before latent issues emerge. |
| **SPA-N-004: Fundamental/Title regime** | Capacity and title warranties subject to the same cap and time limits as general warranties. | Separate, materially higher (ideally price-level) cap and longer period for title, capacity and authority warranties. | **Reject parity with general warranties.** A defect in ownership or authority goes to the core of the 100% share acquisition. |
| **SPA-N-005: Fraud carve-out** | Limitations, exclusive remedy and non-reliance provisions stated to apply to all Claims; no express fraud carve-out identified. | Expressly exclude fraud (including fraudulent misrepresentation) and deliberate concealment from caps, baskets, time bars, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance protections, to the extent legally effective. | **Require an express fraud carve-out.** General limitations should not protect a party against its own fraud. |
| **SPA-N-006: Disclosure scope** | General disclosure of the data room, Accounts, statutory registers and public corporate records, including indexed material as at a stated time. | Specific, fair disclosure against each warranty, with enough detail to identify the nature and scope of the matter; no blanket data-room or public-record disclosure. | **Reject blanket general disclosure; require specific disclosure and an agreed indexed record.** The letter sweeps in DD-002–DD-012 without tying facts to particular warranties or their significance. |
| **SPA-N-007: Buyer knowledge qualifier** | No claim for matters known to the Buyer or advisers, including matters discoverable in the data room or public records. | No general imputation of adviser knowledge or constructive/discoverable knowledge; at most, a narrow actual-knowledge exception for named individuals and specified matters, subject to negotiation. | **Reject the clause as drafted.** Deeming all discoverable information known could nullify warranties despite the Seller’s disclosure burden. |
| **SPA-N-008: Bluefen consent** | Seller to use reasonable endeavours; consent treated as satisfied on delivery of written consent. Disclosure says final consent and evidence of conditions are absent. | A condition to Completion requiring valid written consent and satisfaction or waiver of all conditions; a termination right if not obtained by the long-stop date. | **Make consent an express, unsatisfied condition to Completion.** Bluefen represents about 30% of FY26 revenue and the disclosed consent conditions remain unverified. |
| **SPA-N-009: Riverlark facility** | Approximately AUD 3.2m facility to be addressed by a release after Completion. Disclosure says it remains outstanding and no final discharge is included. | Repayment or refinancing at or before Completion, lender payout evidence, release of all security and related guarantees, and appropriate funds-flow/debt adjustments. | **Do not accept a post-Completion release as sufficient.** The Buyer should not acquire the Company with the debt or security unresolved. |
| **SPA-N-010: Employee bonuses** | AUD 420,000 DD-005 bonuses not separately itemised in funds flow; Seller treats them as its matter. Disclosure confirms they are conditional and excludes any conclusion on payroll tax, superannuation or on-costs. | Confirm amount, triggers and accrued liabilities; specify who funds them and how payroll tax, super and on-costs are treated in the price/funds flow; obtain appropriate warranty or indemnity. | **Require a complete, agreed funds-flow treatment and protection for all related liabilities.** The stated bonuses are omitted and total exposure may exceed AUD 420,000. |
| **SPA-N-011: Ironquay IP indemnity** | Existing indemnity limited to the specific SOW3 payment. DD-004 says transfer of Project Materials depends on cleared payment of every SOW3 fee; DD-010 records AUD 180,000 open, but no receipt or confirmatory assignment is disclosed. | Ensure the Buyer receives valid, complete rights to the Project Materials and related IP; require payment/assignment evidence before Completion and a specific indemnity covering non-transfer, infringement and resulting loss. | **Expand the protection and make evidence of cleared payment and assignment a Completion deliverable.** The disclosed record does not establish that the contractual transfer condition has been met. |
| **SPA-N-012: Export/privacy incident** | Seller calls DD-006 preliminary and not expected to be material; no tailored remedy stated. Disclosure records a link sent to an unintended address, potentially involving about 1,240 records, with access and notification questions unresolved. | Full incident facts, investigation and remediation; compliance and notification warranties; a specific indemnity for incident-related claims, response costs and regulatory liabilities, with appropriate survival and cap treatment. | **Require targeted diligence and specific contractual protection; do not dismiss it as immaterial.** Access, scope and notification remain unresolved. |
| **SPA-N-013: Sandbar renewals** | Three renewals of AUD 110,000 each (AUD 330,000 aggregate) characterised as ordinary-course operating costs. | Establish whether they are executed, unavoidable, terminable, accrued or future commitments; reflect any pre-Completion accrued liabilities in the agreed price mechanics and obtain appropriate disclosure/warranty coverage. | **Require contract-level review and accurate liability treatment before Completion.** The disclosure does not establish that the commitments are ordinary-course or unavoidable. |
| **SPA-N-014: Category separation** | Limitations, exclusive remedy and non-reliance apply to all Claims; Seller says tax and IP fall under the general regime. | Distinct regimes for general warranties, fundamental/title, tax, specific indemnities and fraud, with tailored caps, baskets and survival periods. | **Reject a one-size-fits-all regime.** These categories carry different risks and should not all be diluted by general warranty limitations. |
| **SPA-N-015: Title verification** | Seller relies on DD-012 share register as evidence Harbourglass holds 100% of issued shares. | Verify issued capital, legal and beneficial ownership, encumbrances and authority; require title warranties and delivery of executed transfer instruments and updated register at Completion. | **Treat DD-012 as a source, not completed verification.** The disclosure itself does not establish the Buyer’s independent verification or unencumbered title. |
| **SPA-N-016: Tax/IP open terms** | Seller considers tax and IP settled under the general regime. | Negotiate express tax warranties and a tax indemnity with suitable survival and cap; obtain IP ownership, licence, infringement and chain-of-title protections, plus tailored protection for identified IP risks. | **Keep tax and IP open and negotiate them expressly.** The Seller’s assertion does not resolve terms, and the Ironquay disclosure identifies an unverified transfer condition. |
=== END ADVICE ===
